# Question answer: generator shortcuts

**Task:** `33275a4aae3e`, generator version `2.1.0`. Final generator SHA-256:
`2b77752aa819ff3d2e1b5214f698055365f4ed747cd083baed087d97751fe67f`.

## Which plausible wrong rules fit the canonical evidence?

Two natural alternatives fit **every usable labeled canonical pair**:

1. **Complete-rectangle filling:** preserve foreground, make a zero red only
   when it lies inside a complete axis-aligned foreground rectangle, and make
   other zeros green.
2. **Eight-neighbor exterior:** classify background using diagonal as well as
   orthogonal flood-fill steps, instead of the intended four-neighbor steps.

The complete-rectangle rule is the strongest geometric shortcut identified in
this review: it handles the demonstrated internal stubs without recovering
general enclosure. Eight-neighbor flood fill is a separate adjacency mistake.
Both match **8 canonical records across 2 variants, representing 4 distinct
inputs**. The original eight profiles construct rectangular ladders, so their
geometry never distinguishes either rule. The final probe confirms both rivals
still match all 24 sampled legacy-profile cases.
Evidence: [final probe](checks/shortcut-probe-final/report.json).

## What exact lawful input distinguishes them?

Start with a **22×25 zero grid**, then paint color **8** along these inclusive,
zero-based segments. Horizontal tuples are `(row,left,right)`; vertical tuples
are `(column,top,bottom)`:

```text
H = [(4,3,18), (7,0,8), (10,9,18), (13,2,13), (16,2,15)]
V = [(5,1,19), (14,1,12), (11,8,20)]
```

This input passes the generator validator. It has one connected network,
5 horizontal strokes, 3 vertical strokes, 9 crossings, no elbows or
T-junctions, and three enclosed four-connected components of sizes **48, 10,
and 4**. Density is `96/550`; only the left canvas boundary is touched.

Public Racket execution under unchanged rule hash `a7f4d11b444d` returns 8 on
every stroke, 2 at exactly the following positions, and 3 everywhere else:

| Rows | Columns containing output 2 | Rectangle rival gets these wrong |
|---|---|---|
| 5–6 | 6–13 | Yes |
| 7 | 9–13 | Yes |
| 8–9 | 6–10 and 12–13 | Yes |
| 10 | 6–8 | Yes |
| 11–12 | 6–10 and 12–13 | Yes |
| 14–15 | 6–10 | No |

The rectangle rival therefore makes **52 errors**, predicting 3 where the
reference returns 2. The eight-neighbor rival makes exactly **4 errors**, at
`(11,12)`, `(11,13)`, `(12,12)`, and `(12,13)`: its diagonal escape through
`(13,14)` is illegal under four-neighbor connectivity.

The [task-local counterexample](repo/generators/33275a4aae3e/counterexamples/stepped-diagonal-seal.json)
contains the complete grids, predictions, coordinates, recipe, source/rule
hashes, and verified receipt links. The authoritative output is retained in
[apply-000.json](checks/shortcut-probe-final/apply-000.json), result 38.

## Does the repaired generator actually produce counterexamples?

Yes. The two new profiles, `stepped_l_22x25` and `stepped_r_22x25`, produce
parameterized stepped enclosures with diagonal seals. The final probe executed
all 10 profiles in each of three bands at seed 17/index 4: **30 distinct
generated inputs and outputs**. All six stepped cases refute both shortcuts;
all 39 checked inputs, including canonical and handmade cases, pass their
domain checks. Exact generated replay settings are in the counterexample JSON
and [cases.jsonl](checks/shortcut-probe-final/cases.jsonl). The handmade grid is
identified separately; no claim relies on discovering its exact RNG seed.

Default lessons use three demonstrations and one query with an alternating
period-2 witness/legacy schedule. Four consecutive indices contain two witness
inputs, so holding out any one leaves a witness among the demonstrations.
Together with the nontrivial interior/exterior coloring, this excludes the
five declared rivals. The completed final census found **zero ambiguity in
300 lessons and 1,200 one-query rotations**, with 1,200 unique inputs.
[Census summary](checks/lesson-census-final.summary.json).

This guarantee is relative to those five rivals and contiguous default
sampling. Explicit non-null profile overrides can remove witness coverage;
`scene_profile=None` now behaves like omission. Arbitrary unknown hypotheses,
external filtering, and arbitrary subsets of generated pairs remain outside
the claim.
